and rescue the Arabs from the edge of the sword,
saying, "Behold, Emperor Basil himself is swooping down upon you!"
And spies came again,
and reported the very same thing to him.
Therefore fear fell upon the army of the Egyptians,
and they abandoned all their baggage,
and fled, each man upon a single horse.
And the Romans arrived,
and plundered everything that they found.
And Abu'l-Fada'il and Lu'lu' went out to pay homage to Emperor Basil,
and presented gifts to him.
And he departed and went and captured the fortress of Shayzar {OCR: Sayrin}.
And from there he went and captured Homs,
and carried away captive from it more than ten thousand souls.
And from there he went to Tripoli,
and encamped against it for forty days,
and was not able to conquer it;
so he left it and went to his own land.
Now al-Aziz, the caliph of Egypt, when he heard these things,
was greatly distressed,
and gathered numerous troops,
intending to come in person and capture Aleppo.
And because the disease of colic was constantly happening to him,
in one whole year he was scarcely able to come from Egypt to Bilbays, a distance of ten parasangs,
and there he died.
And after him reigned his son al-Hakim, as caliph over Egypt and the West, in the year 386
of the Arabs [996 AD].
And at this time Isa bar Nestorius was killed in Egypt,
and in his place was appointed as proxiomos a certain Jacobite man,
whose name was Abu'l-Ala Fahd ibn Ibrahim, an Egyptian {Copt}.
This man was the legal secretary of Barjawan, the white eunuch commander-in-chief,
and he promoted him.
At this time Christians,
without having to change their confession,
were appointed viziers in the laughing {OCR? / prominent} kingdom of the Egyptians.
And it is not so in our own times;
for now,
unless they embrace Islam,
they are not entrusted with the vizierate.
And in the year 387
of the Arabs [997 AD],
which is the year 1308
of the Greeks [997 AD],
(997 of our Lord?):
the Dux Domesticus of the Romans came and encamped against Apamea.
And he pressed it hard with famine,
until a dog was sold in it for two gold dinars.
Then came Ibn Samsamah, the commander-in-chief of the Egyptian Arabs,
to enter into the fortress and defend it.
And the Romans pursued him,
and killed about two thousand men of the Arabs,
and the rest began to flee.
